title: Question 2
stem:
A liquid of density ρ fills a container to a depth h, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
The base of the container has area A.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Derive, from the definitions of pressure and density, the equation $p = \rho gh$
where p is the pressure exerted by the liquid on the base of the container and g is the acceleration of free fall.

markscheme_points.text: ρ = m / V or ρ = m / Ah
p = F / A or p = W / A
p = [ρAhg] / A or p = [ρVg] / [V / h] (so) p = ρgh

hints: Hint 1: Consider the physical mechanism underlying this process based on pressure definition and units.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
Hint 3: Check your intermediate calculation steps carefully and ensure your final answer is stated to an appropriate number of significant figures with correct SI units.
parts.proper_answer: ρ = m / V or ρ = m / Ah; p = F / A or p = W / A; p = [ρAhg] / A or p = [ρVg] / [V / h] (so) p = ρgh
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
Identify the core physical principle governing this problem: Pressure definition and units. State the relevant formula or theoretical relationship clearly.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Substitute the known quantities into the formula with correct SI units and powers of ten:
$$ρ = m / V or ρ = m / Ah; p = F / A or p = W / A; p = [ρAhg] / A or p = [ρVg] / [V / h] (so) p = ρgh$$
Work through the intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.text:
determine the density of liquid M.
density = $kg m ^{3} $
hints: Hint 1: Identify the given data from the problem and recall the governing equation connecting these quantities using density formula.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
Identify the core physical principle governing this problem: Density formula. State the relevant formula or theoretical relationship clearly.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Substitute the known quantities into the formula with correct SI units and powers of ten:
$$(∆)p = ρg(∆)h (9.15 - 9.10) × 104 = ρ × 9.81 × (0.17 - 0.10); ρ = 730 (728) kg m-3$$
Work through the intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
